an.leaksIntro: Results are EV-adjusted: in all-in hands the all-in EV replaces the actual result, so single coinflips do not create findings. {tested} spots checked; false alarms are corrected for all of them together (Benjamini–Hochberg): likely means a false-discovery rate under 5 %, possible under 20 %.

an.tip.bb_defence: On average your calls from the big blind end worse than folding would have. Call less with offsuit hands that are easily dominated (e.g. KJo, QTo, A8o) against early positions, 3-bet your strongest hands instead of calling, and do not pay off to the river with one pair out of position.
an.tip.sb_complete: From the small blind you play out of position for the whole hand. Raise or fold instead of completing.
an.tip.sb_flat: Calling from the small blind invites the big blind in and leaves you out of position. 3-bet or fold more.
an.guide.fold_to_3bet: rough guide: around half; above 70 % opponents can 3-bet you with anything
an.tip.fold_to_3bet: You fold most of the time when your open is re-raised. Open a little tighter from early positions so you have hands to continue with, and with 20-40 BB answer more 3-bets with an all-in or a call.
an.tip.depth10: At 10-15 BB most hands should be all-in or fold. Avoid raising and folding, and avoid calling.
an.tip.depth25: At 25-40 BB re-shoving all-in over an open is often the best play. Calling and playing after the flop with this stack loses for you.
an.tip.depth40: With a deep stack small edges after the flop decide. Review the biggest losses: were they one-pair hands paid off to the river?
an.tip.depth: Review the biggest losses at this stack depth.
an.tip.positionBTN: The button should be your best seat. Fewer calls, more raises, and keep betting when checked to.
an.tip.position: Play a little tighter from this seat.
an.tip.hand: With this many hands a result depends mostly on a few big pots. Look at those pots: was it a dominated hand calling a raise?

lp.title: How luck is calculated
lp.allin: An all-in here means: all the chips are in the middle, cards are still to come, and nobody can act any more. From that moment the result depends only on the cards that are dealt, so it is a clean measure of luck.
lp.equity: Equity: your share of the pot if this exact situation were played out over and over. It is not estimated: the app goes through every possible remaining board (up to 1,712,304 of them preflop) with the real cards of everyone involved. Ties split the pot, and side pots are handled.
lp.ev: Expected (EV): equity × pot, minus what you put in. What you win on average in this spot.
lp.luck: Luck = actual − expected. Positive: you won more than the cards deserved. Negative: less.
lp.badge: The dashboard sums the luck of every all-in in the period and compares it with how much that luck could swing by chance: an all-in with 50% equity for a big pot swings a lot, one with 95% equity hardly at all. The result is the number of "typical swings" your luck is away from zero.
lp.levels: Very lucky: +1.5 or more · Lucky: +0.5 to +1.5 · Average: between −0.5 and +0.5 · Bad run: −0.5 to −1.5 · Worst run: −1.5 or less. Two lost coinflips are "Average"; losing a series of 80% all-ins is a bad run. With fewer than 20 all-ins the badge says the sample is small.
lp.bb: Everything is counted in big blinds, so an all-in at 25/50 weighs the same as the same all-in at 500/1,000. Under the badge the app says how rare your result is for a player with average luck, e.g. "a run this bad or worse happens to about 1 in 6 players" (from the normal distribution: −1 typical swing or worse is about 16%).
lp.moment: Luck always uses the equity at the moment of the all-in. The replayer also shows how the equity changes as the flop, turn and river come, but those numbers are only for watching; they do not change your luck.
lp.example: You have {aa} against {kk}, 100 BB each, all-in before the flop. Your equity is about 81%.
lp.exampleMath: Expected = 0.81 × 200 − 100 = +62 BB. If you win: actual +100 BB, luck +38 BB. If you lose: actual −100 BB, luck −162 BB.
lp.reading: Good decisions show up as a positive expected number: you get your chips in as the favourite. Luck swings up and down and tends towards zero over many tournaments. The orange line on the dashboard is your result with that luck removed.
lp.limits: Limits: measured in chips and big blinds, not dollars (no payout structures needed). Only all-ins where every player's cards are known count, as in PokerTracker. A "bad beat" is losing with 80%+ equity, a "suckout" winning with 20% or less.

cashed.tip: In bounty tournaments the summary gives only the total won and hand histories hold no bounty payouts, so place money and bounties cannot be told apart.
places.tip: Your place divided by the number of players, from the summaries. No payout structure is assumed. With a late registration, players who busted before you sat down count in the field, so the share looks better than against the players you actually met.
places.title: Where you finish
places.intro: Your final place as a share of the field ({tournaments} with a place). The line marks where a player of average skill lands: in each band in proportion to its width.
lp.itm: ITM (in the money) is shown only for tournaments without bounties and for satellites (a ticket counts). In a bounty tournament the summary gives only the total you received and the hand histories hold no bounty payouts, so money for your place cannot be told apart from knockouts: there the app shows Cashed (place or bounty). Top 10 % / 15 % of the field are plain facts: your final place divided by the number of players, with a 95 % interval over tournaments. No payout structure is assumed anywhere.
places.introSplit: Your final place as a share of the field. The line marks where a player of average skill lands (in each band in proportion to its width); it is shown only for entries from the start.
places.lateNote: No comparison with an average player here: players who busted before you sat down count in the field, so these places look better than they are.
